input_spelling_aliases: Funastrum cynanchodies — typo from Master Plant Pool row 489, represents same accepted taxon
taxonomic_note: Kew POWO and 2023 Flora of North America accept F. cynanchoides as distinct from F. crispum and F. heterophyllum. Historical usage F. cynanchoides subsp. hartwegii generally relates to F. heterophyllum in Flora of North America; avoid using such source images on this card until concepts are reconciled.
look_here_first: Look at an OPPOSITE HEART-BASED LEAF with generally FLAT (not wavy) margins, then follow its axil to a clustered UMBEL of little creamy to rosy pink star flowers with a GLOSSY WHITE five-part corona in the center. The flowers are relatively SMALL, with petals about 3–6 mm, unlike large brown/orange F. crispum corollas (~20mm across).

project_inclusion.source_pool: My iNaturalist Flora; LBJ Hays County Natives; Personal List
project_inclusion.range_basis: Native to Texas according to Kew POWO/FNA and source-pool Hays native designation; preserve UNRESOLVED until target-county native certification. Source pool approval does not itself count as independent 3-county proof.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Perennial twining milkweed vine with white latex and slender flexible stems (no tendrils).
morphology_keys.stems: Thin, often sprawling/twining green stems; fine short curved trichomes occur on stems and flower stalks.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite simple petiolate blades often ovate, lanceolate, or slightly arrow-shaped and typically cordate at base; widest variable ~0.7–4.5 cm; margins usually PLANE rather than crispate or strongly wavy.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Axillary umbel-like cymes, sometimes appearing as rounded bouquet of many little flowers; compare size of ONE open flower rather than head size alone.
morphology_keys.flowers: Cream/white or rose-tinged five-lobed spreading corolla, petal lobes ~3–6mm, often pink at tips and fringed/ciliate at petal margins. Corolla inner face can be minutely hispidulous to nearly smooth (Flora of North America).
morphology_keys.corona: Five glossy white swollen ovoid corona lobes around the milkweed gynostegium, often with cream/green/pink base; central coronas are NOT unopened flower buds or petals.
morphology_keys.fruit: Usually lone slender oblong to lanceolate follicle ~6–9cm long, curved-hairy, with 20–50 brown winged seeds bearing silky coma.
best_field_traits: cream-to-pink small five-petaled stars in umbel-like heads
five plump brilliant white oval corona lobes
mostly flat-edged cordate ovate-lanceolate opposite leaves
thin twining stems with white latex
seeds in slender follicle with white silky coma
field_id_sequence: Locate opposite leaf pair; do not mistake twining growth for a tendril.
Photograph one mature leaf including margin and heart-shaped/arrow-like base.
Photo an entire rounded axillary cluster, then ONE individual bloom at scale.
Check the WHITE bulging five-part corona inside pinkish/cream corolla; compare larger browner F. crispum.
If out of flower, photograph follicle and stem hairs for additional checks.
cautions: Strong pink/purple flowers on extremely narrow leaves in western deserts can be F. heterophyllum; older records call it a subspecies of cynanchoides.
Don't identify this species solely from common name 'climbing milkweed'; F. crispum also climbs.
At an early stage latex and opposite leaves resemble Cynanchum, Matelea and Gonolobus; use central flower anatomy.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against F. crispum: typical leaves have flatter margins, cream to rosy smaller corollas, and unconstricted swollen glossy white corona lobes; crispum often crisped leaves, large browner/orange blooms and constricted corona lobes. Against talayote: Funastrum flowers are usually more visibly star-shaped in tight umbel-like round clusters; talayote has many tiny green-and-white flowers arranged in branchlike axillary inflorescences. Against Matelea: Funastrum lacks the reticulated flat green floral mesh and shiny silver central pearl of M. reticulata.
